chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'In the case of a man who made the divorce of his wife in the hands of two men, and one of them divorced her but the other refused, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) rejected that until they both gathered together on the divorce.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce when delegated to two agents who do not agree?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) preference for joint agency (*tawafuq*) in delegated divorce, ensuring that the irrevocability of the act is not triggered by a single agent's unilateral decision. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on clarity and mutual consent in dissolving marital bonds, distinguishing this conditional delegation from standard unilateral divorce. The ruling underscores the principle that when authority is shared, its exercise typically requires concurrence unless specified otherwise.
